observations.finding: Treated colonies are more compact and cohesive with smoother, rounder perimeters and more rounded/less spread cell shapes than the more dispersed, flattened DMSO sheets. Cells have shorter major axis.
Visible colony circularity and solidity appears increased vs DMSO; peripheral F-actin red cortical belt appears continuous around tight colonies, consistent with compact morphology.
Nuclei stained blue with DNA stain appear on average smaller in area and shorter in major axis in treated fields vs DMSO. Not quantified from composite alone beyond visual size comparison.
Nuclei appear more elongated/eccentric and slightly more irregular in contour than round DMSO nuclei; eccentricity visibly higher.

Apparent fraction of closely apposed/binucleate nuclei within dense colonies appears higher vs DMSO, with occasional paired nuclei in one cell territory; true multinucleation difficult to resolve from tight packing in composite at this magnification. Consistent with segmentation proxy increase from 0.257 to 0.48-0.56, not visual count.

Absolute frequency of strikingly large/giant nuclei is low in both control and treated; no widespread polyploid giant cells obvious. Small absolute increase 0.006 to 0.025-0.028 in frac_large_nucleus is not conspicuous visually.

No obvious loss of F-actin red signal or beta-tubulin green signal vs DMSO in composite: red cortical F-actin still present around colonies, green tubulin diffuse cytoplasmic present in both. No bundles, asters, or depolymerization obvious at this resolution.

Overall confluence/coverage in 10uM fields shows more empty black background than DMSO/1uM fields, suggesting lower cell number at highest concentration, but DMSO cell count not provided for direct comparison and composite only.

Phenotype is smaller, more eccentric nuclei with compact round colonies and increased adjacency proxy - not specific to listed MoAs. Measurements confirm smaller nuc_area/major_axis, higher eccentricity, higher roundness/solidity, modest large-nucleus increase without visual giants.

reflection.text:
Truth unblinded: AZ-J = Epithelial. Protocol NSC 4/4 Epithelial (10 uM 0.802, 1 uM 0.862, 0.3 uM 0.713, 0.1 uM 0.455; summed similarity 2.831) - verdict correct, scientist and agent both Epithelial p=0.86 approve.

What got it right:
- compare_to_reference_atlas was decisive. e5: 2/2 Epithelial (k=10: Epithelial 5/10 mean 0.771 vs Protein synthesis 4/10 mean 0.532, Eg5 1/10). e8: 4/4 Epithelial over 4 acquired wells same k-distribution. Unanimous vote held from high dose through low dose, not a single-well artifact.
- Dose trend for epithelial morphology, not generic toxicity. dose_response e10 nuc_eccentricity rho=+1.00 p=0 and e11 cell_roundness rho=+1.00 p=0 across 4 wells (10, 1, 0.3, 0.1 uM) showed monotone compact round colony phenotype from 0.1 uM upward. Cell counts remained high (503, 847, 285, 422 cells) despite microscopist note "density lower vs DMSO" in e4, arguing against acute toxicity-driven compaction.
- Visual corroboration in e4: 4 fields described as compact cohesive round colonies with smaller, more eccentric nuclei. This anchored the z-scores: e2 nuc_major_axis z=-8.8, e3 z=-7.3 with nuc_eccentricity z=+7.9/+7.7, i.e. smaller not giant nuclei. That directly contradicted Aurora/Eg5 expectation of large polyploid nuclei and mitotic figures. Hypothesis update correctly down-weighted Aurora 0.02, Eg5 0.02, Actin 0.01, Microtubule destabilizers/stabilizers 0.01 each for preserved F-actin/tubulin patterns.
- Chemical lookup e14 after review correctly returned no PubChem/ChEMBL structure or curated mechanisms for BBBC021 internal code AZ-J, so we did not over-interpret a chemical prior and relied on phenotype, which was appropriate.

What misled / what we missed and why:
- frac_multinucleate_proxy was the strongest confounder: e2 z=+8.0, e3 z=+10.9, e6 z=+9.0, e7 z=+3.9, plus e6 frac_large_nucleus z=+6.3. Taken alone this mimics Aurora/Eg5 polyploidization/multinucleation and explains the 1/10 Eg5 neighbour and Protein synthesis 4/10 neighbours in the atlas. e9 dose_response rho=+0.40 p=0.6 showed no monotone dose dependence for this feature, unlike the epithelial shape features, which should have flagged artifact.
- Acquisition choice amplified this: we sampled only rep 1 at 4 doses (10, 1, 0.3, 0.1 uM) and skipped the 4 lowest doses (0.003-0.03 uM range from e1) and all replicates. Review correctly notes replicate independence is weak; we compensated with the 4-point monotone trend but cannot estimate well-to-well variance at a given dose. Low-dose similarity 0.455 at 0.1 uM was near threshold and would have benefited from a replicate.
- describe_phenotype e4 was under-specified in the tool summary ("8 observations; candidates: unknown") - we had to rely on review critique's paraphrase of compact cohesive morphology to resolve the multinucleate proxy as segmentation artifact of tightly packed epithelial colonies, not true multinucleation. Without that visual, the z-scores alone would have favored mitotic failure.
- Literature search e15 for MCF7 epithelial morphology/E-cadherin returned 0 hits, and e16 phenotypic screening classification returned 4 hits including general Cell Painting profiling work (e.g., PMID 41160542). No paper directly supported AZ-J epithelial mechanism, so our conclusion rested entirely on NSC + dose morphology, which was correct but left the 0.86 probability with residual Protein synthesis uncertainty appropriately.

Why the call succeeded: we used two sequential atlas comparisons and dose_response trends to de-weight a high but non-monotone multinucleate proxy in favor of monotone eccentricity/roundness + smaller nuclei + unanimous NSC, consistent with standard Cell Painting NSC majority-vote phenomics approaches (PMID 41160542).
